scores.why: A gives relevant insurance templates, named blocks and authoring deliverables, whereas B leaves the blocks generic and reopens the mandated CDN choice, C leaves its Core Components approach to Edge Delivery unclear, and D describes the platforms without a concrete template catalog or clear deployment responsibilities.

D inventories pages and PDFs, assigns retirement decisions to Compliance and tests old filing URLs, while A and B offer useful but generic imports and redirects without a PDF or filing retention method, and C spends substantial space on platform capabilities rather than migration controls.

C provides accessibility acceptance criteria, automated merge checks, manual release testing and PDF triage despite excluding PDF tagging, D provides credible WCAG testing but less explicit release enforcement and no PDF plan, and A and B discuss authoring setup without answering accessibility.

C distinguishes field Core Web Vitals thresholds from release scores and provides baselines and tag controls, B offers tailored performance gates but relies heavily on an absolute Lighthouse target, A largely promises continuous testing without implementation detail, and D does not address performance.

C directly retains Akamai and specifies caching, purging, security headers and verification, B gives useful origin-cache and invalidation details but leaves the header configuration unspecified, A substitutes general site construction and optional CDN selection, and D barely addresses the mandatory configuration.

A defines routed Compliance approvals and deliverables but adds separately licensed Workfront and leaves approval enforcement insufficiently demonstrated, D proposes roles and governance checks without a concrete regulated-page publication gate, B lists integrations and extra dependencies instead of an implemented approval flow, and C addresses block authoring rather than approvals.

D supplies quote-start variants, Compliance review, persistent allocation and outcome measurement but leaves the Akamai assignment mechanism underspecified, C supplies a credible experiment plan and tracking without explaining allocation or confirming experimentation entitlements, and A and B do not describe A/B testing.

B best addresses Drupal, Akamai, filing URLs, content freeze and hypercare but still lacks concrete traffic-switching and rollback execution, while A and D provide nearly identical generic checklists with only rollback criteria, and C mixes a useful freeze plan with platform setup details and similarly thin search and rollback controls.

A defines a tailored prompt portfolio, competitor baseline, answer inspection and report deliverables, D explains monitored visibility metrics but concentrates its implementation on traffic data, and B and C largely measure bot activity and referrals rather than how assistants describe Cedar Prairie.

D connects observed answer gaps to approved insurance content and third-party outreach deliverables although the outreach method remains thin, A and B provide effectively equivalent on-site publishing programs without third-party work, and C adds monitoring context and quantified content output but still omits off-site improvement.

C directly designs approved auto, home and life comparisons leading to quote-start pages but introduces an extra handoff license, A and D provide credible generic launch and testing steps without the requested comparison or quote journey, and B adds a potentially unnecessary Qualifier dependency while leaving those core journeys unspecified.

B specifies an approved source register, superseded-filing exclusion, prohibited rate and claim decisions, secure-channel referrals and repeat testing, whereas A gives general grounding and refusal assurances, C gives a generic implementation checklist, and D adds source restrictions without defining the regulated-topic rules.

C addresses Genesys routing, context, after-hours handling and end-to-end testing but leaves bridge implementation and failed-transfer recovery unclear while adding Qualifier, B promises only a generic handoff, and A and D substitute analytics for the requested contact-center integration.

A defines question topics, drop-offs and quote starts with a shared-identity validation plan but leaves the underlying event instrumentation thin, B describes dashboard capabilities without delivering the requested funnel, and C and D offer equivalent generic conversation and purchase reporting rather than the specified insurance measures.

D covers all four channels with schemas, identity stitching, data views and test customers although the identity prerequisites need more detail, while A mainly describes product capabilities and B and C implement only a Concierge-centered subset without Marketo or agent ingestion.

A supplies a concrete Snowflake change-capture plan with joins, reconciliation and update/delete tests, B adds useful sensitive-data governance but fewer validation steps, C gives the core configuration without accountable verification or effort, and D promises reconciliation without detailing its execution or tailoring the source setup.

A addresses consented activity flowing into Salesforce and estimates both directions but leaves Salesforce-to-CJA implementation largely in deliverables, B and C provide credible scheduled CRM ingestion while omitting the outbound website and Concierge flow, and D also omits that flow while spending space on unrelated monthly answer reviews.

D gives Power BI-specific dashboard scope, access, query constraints and reconciliation deliverables, A provides a sound connection and validation plan with limits but remains generic across tools, B omits those limits, and C provides only a brief setup commitment with no effort or dashboard delivery detail.

C connects the existing site, forms, identities and Marketo ingestion to CJA with sample reconciliation but assumes a more expensive stitching package without comparing alternatives, B covers the analytics route but not the website connection, and A and D largely reprovision existing email infrastructure without implementing CJA integration.

B provides tailored nonpublic-data classification and access deliverables but leaves consent enforcement, retention and activation controls incomplete, C provides consent gating and withdrawal testing but limited concrete GLBA storage controls, D addresses only audience-use approval, and A largely substitutes analytics and activation for privacy implementation.

C trains all three requested roles on their actual work and supplies practical checks, recordings and role-specific guides, A and B provide substantially equivalent author-only programs that omit Compliance and analysts, and D substitutes Coworker and developer activities for the requested enablement.

A covers permissions, reusable workflows, testing, all 35 users and ongoing adoption with explicit effort, B stops at workflow definition, and C and D offer useful but substantially equivalent pilot training without explaining setup or the wider rollout.

D covers monthly releases, monitoring, source freshness and answer testing but leaves the expressly requested support hours and response times as an unfilled placeholder, B and C provide only conversation sampling services, and A offers no meaningful ongoing service plan.

B combines a stable prompt cohort, visibility trends, prioritized actions and quantified approved content delivery, A and D provide substantially equivalent content services without Brand Visibility reporting despite different effort estimates, and C distinguishes useful measures but lacks a concrete monthly reporting service.

notes: All 96 presented answers fall within their displayed word limits under ordinary word counting, and only the 24 requirements with answer blocks were scored.
Repeated platform descriptions and adjacent-service checklists often fail to answer the actual requirement, so their length and technical terminology did not earn extra credit.

The strongest answers connect Cedar Prairie's regulated content, existing systems and requested outcomes to concrete deliverables and validation, but many still omit operational mechanisms or scope boundaries.

Separately licensed Workfront, Qualifier and higher analytics packages weaken answers where their necessity and fit with the selected stack are not established; unverified product capabilities were treated as uncertainty rather than asserted factual errors.

Most schedules remain generic build or launch references rather than commitments to the ten- and twelve-month deadlines, and the ongoing support answer with otherwise broad coverage retains an unresolved hours-and-response-times placeholder.
